functional.title: Dispute intake and policy versions
functional.definition: Freeze tenant-scoped input hash, consent scope, label vocabulary, guideline revision and original dataset version. Deduplicate replayed submissions.

functional.title: Reviewer enrollment and conflicts
functional.definition: Store opt-in, language eligibility, calibration expiry, organization link and conflict exclusions. Expose aliases to dataset operators.

functional.title: Paid assignments and leases
functional.definition: Reserve slot budgets, issue scoped task offers, record delivery entitlements and reconcile payment references. Disclose pay before reviewer acceptance.

functional.title: Blind reviewer workbench
functional.definition: Implement a per-assignment view, draft save and one final versioned opinion with rationale; expire leases and invalidate stale views.

functional.title: Agreement and adjudication
functional.definition: Apply a deterministic routing policy after both valid opinions; present conflicting rationales to a qualified expert with an abstain action.

functional.title: QA patch and provenance
functional.definition: Produce a deterministic diff pinned to the input version and case decisions, require dataset QA approval and support superseding rulings.

functional.title: Calibration, reporting and recovery
functional.definition: Build per-cohort calibration and cost reports, work expiry handling, reviewer payout reconciliation and replay over a clean database snapshot.

nonfunctional.title: Replayable evidence
nonfunctional.definition: A reviewer can reproduce the outcome from the exact input revision, actor scope, persisted decision and redacted evidence reference after a process restart.

invariants.title: Dispute intake and policy versions
invariants.definition: A policy change cannot alter an already-open case.

invariants.title: Reviewer enrollment and conflicts
invariants.definition: Assignments honor the policy's required identity and conflict evidence.

invariants.title: Paid assignments and leases
invariants.definition: The two initial assignments and any expert purchase together stay within the authorized cap.

invariants.title: Blind reviewer workbench
invariants.definition: Peer labels, original labels and identifying peer metadata remain hidden during blind review.

invariants.title: Agreement and adjudication
invariants.definition: Different or abstaining labels cannot silently produce a training label.

invariants.title: QA patch and provenance
invariants.definition: Only accepted resolved decisions target matching source item hashes.

invariants.title: Calibration, reporting and recovery
invariants.definition: Counts distinguish resolved, unresolved, paid and pending independently; majority agreement is not labeled ground truth.
